texts.preamble: Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Author: Chief Justice Bench: Bhaskar Bhattacharya, J.B.Pardiwala Ilaben Pathakv/Sstate Of Gujarat C/Ca/10442/2012 Cav Order
texts.facts: By our order dated 29th December, 2011, we appointed a Committee of Commissioners taking into consideration the alarming situation, which was prevailing in the city of Ahmedabad and some of the areas on the outskirts. We appointed a Committee comprising of nine Commissioners, headed by Dr. Dileep Mavalankar, Dean (Academics), Indian Institute of Public Health, Gandhinagar, with a request to assist us on the following issues: a) To take stock of the affairs and prevailing conditions of the Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad, regarding the unhygienic conditions of the hospital that led to numerous deaths due to Dengue and Malaria in the past nine months and also situation regarding these issues in other government hospitals of the city. b) To take complete details and information regarding deaths due to Dengue, Malaria and Falciparum and then identify form the record the exact problems that gave rise to such situations leading to deaths of resident doctors, nursing staff and patients in the Civil Hospital. c) To give a report on the overall administration of the Civil Hospital regarding the sanitation measures, quarantine measures and disposal of bio-medical waste taken by the Civil Hospital. d) To apply the same methodology to other government hospitals in the State and identify giving rise to such kind of deaths due to Dengue and malaria in hospitals. e) To recommend appropriate measures or a proper structure for regulating the Government hospital system. f) To evaluate the extent of the problem caused due to unhygienic conditions in the Civil Hospital and other government hospitals of the State and negligence of the administration in maintaining cleanliness in the hospitals including other parts of the city and recommend measures required to deal with the problem effectively. g) To recommend steps to be taken by the Health Department and Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation to tackle the problem of Dengue and Malaria. h) To consider and suggest any other issue incidental to the above issues. Ilaben Pathak & vs State Of Gujarat & on 30 April, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18239292/ 4 2. Pursuant to our order dated 29th December, 2011, the Committee tendered its first preliminary report dated 30th March, 2012, relating to unhygienic conditions in the Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad, leading to the death of a resident doctor, including other public hospitals in the city of Ahmedabad. The Committee in its first preliminary report gave a fair idea about the observations and suggested few short-term recommendations for the purpose of taking precautions during the monsoon of 2012. The Committee however, requested for some more time to complete the work and accordingly, we granted three months time for the purpose of completing the work and filing another report. Thereafter, the Committee tendered a second interim urgent report, taking into consideration the alarming situation which prevailed even during the monsoon of 2012. 3. The Committee, thereafter, has placed its final report dated 4th February, 2013, relating to the unhygienic conditions prevailing in the campus of the Civil Hospital and other public hospitals of the State and in the city of Ahmedabad. 5. On receipt of the copy of the report of the Committee, an affidavit has been filed on behalf of the petitioner highlighting few relevant features of the report of the Committee as well as few suggestions at the end of the petitioner. In the same manner, the Additional Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department of the State Government has also filed an affidavit stating as to what steps have been taken pursuant to the recommendations made by the Committee as well as the precautions which are being taken, taking into consideration that the monsoon is not far. One affidavit has also been filed by the Deputy Municipal Commissioner on behalf of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, highlighting the steps which have been taken by the Corporation to meet with the problems of unhygienic conditions prevailing in the campus of the Civil Hospital as well as other Government hospitals, including the city at large. 8. According to the Committee, the delayed construction of new buildings led to big foundation pits and other pits on the ground, which resulted in blockage of the drains. Heavy construction vehicle movement crushed some of the underground pipelines resulting in stagnation of dirty water at various places in the campus of the Civil Hospital. The Committee also noted that not only the patients from all over the city and the outskirts were admitted suffering from malaria, dengue etc., but some of the staff members who worked round the clock to treat the patients also became victims of malaria and dengue.
texts.arguments: It has been submitted by Mr. P.K. Jani, the learned counsel appearing for the State Government and Mr. S.N. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation that the report of the Committee, more particularly the shortcomings noticed by the Committee have been taken care of to a considerable extent.
texts.petitioner_arguments: It has been submitted by Mr. P.K. Jani, the learned counsel appearing for the State Government and Mr. S.N. Shelat, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation that the report of the Committee, more particularly the shortcomings noticed by the Committee have been taken care of to a considerable extent.
